submission.justification: Based on comprehensive simulation studies across the allowed threshold range (20-60 GeV), Algorithm-L1 with a threshold of 32.5 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.346% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This represents a significant improvement over Algorithm-L2 (peak efficiency ~85.3% at 33 GeV) and Algorithm-L3 (peak efficiency ~75% at 30 GeV). Algorithm-L1 uses iterative topological clustering with learned calibration, which provides superior performance while still fitting within the FPGA resource budget. The 32.5 GeV threshold was determined through systematic scanning and represents the optimal balance between signal acceptance and background rejection at the allocated rate.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 at 32.5 GeV achieves 93.346% signal efficiency, which is the highest among all tested configurations across all three candidate algorithms.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate algorithms in candidate_specs.md (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration).

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be deployable in Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: According to candidate_specs.md, all three algorithms including Algorithm-L1 fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs).
The recommended threshold of 32.5 GeV is within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Operate at the allocated trigger rate of 8 kHz
requirements.evidence: All simulations were performed at the allocated 8 kHz rate as specified in rate_allocation.md, and efficiency is measured at this rate.
